static_traits.name: Lin Jie
static_traits.social_status: Close relationship with family but hesitant to express anxiety; feeling anxious about interpersonal interactions at college with avoidance
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problem experiences yet; has not yet received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, highly cooperative, neutral attitude; speech rate and specific speech characteristics not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: 'I worry that after starting college in the fall, people will think I am strange because I hate spaghetti and will not want to be friends with me.' This belief triggers anxiety and worry, and leads to avoiding socializing and sleep difficulties.
basic_info.core_demands: Fear and anxiety around college social life have become overwhelming and affect daily life; hoping to gain support and relief through counseling.
growth_experiences: Fear and anxiety about college social life began after high school graduation and gradually worsened as the semester approached; when thinking of making new friends or attending social activities, daily recurring worries arise with avoidance of related situations, along with sleep difficulties.

Good academic performance (graduated high school with good grades), planning to attend the University of Michigan in the fall; anticipation about entering a new social environment is the main background triggering anxiety.

core_beliefs: Being different from others, I will be seen as strange and thus not accepted
Others' evaluations determine my worth and belonging

special_situations.event: Thinking about making new friends in college or attending social activities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others learn I do not like spaghetti, they will think I am strange and distance themselves from me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding social situations, trying not to mention one's own food preferences
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am weird and will not want to be friends with me

special_situations.event: As college start approaches, repeatedly thinking about future social situations
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot fit in, I will stay lonely and be excluded
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated worrying, difficulty falling asleep to stay alert
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will be excluded after starting college, left alone

special_situations.event: Realizing the difference in food preferences between oneself and others (not liking spaghetti)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A small difference is enough for others to negate me and not accept me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to suppress worries with self-comfort (telling oneself 'others will not care')
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not fit in and will be seen as strange

special_situations.event: Recalling that no one mocked her food preferences in the past, yet still continuously worrying about future judgment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Unless there is clear evidence proving I will not be judged, I should keep worrying
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring existing positive evidence, continuously maintaining worry for self-protection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Even though no one mocked me in the past, I will be mocked and excluded in college

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted by peers, integrate into the group, and build friendships
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged, being excluded, and loneliness
defense_goal: Reducing feelings of being rejected and anxiety through avoiding socializing and rational self-comfort

object_relations.object_representation: A peer group that judges and rejects people over small differences

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about college social life, others' evaluations, or imagining how peers might view her 'disliking spaghetti'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will act like picky judges, negating and rejecting her differences (transference: projecting the inner fear of being rejected onto external others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying feelings in a restrained, rationalized tone, emphasizing 'this is not a big deal/most people will not care', offering logical interpretations to avoid deeply expressing fear and vulnerability.

manifestations: Worrying about being seen as 'strange' and not accepted due to a small difference (disliking spaghetti)
Anticipation about building new relationships in college triggers strong anxiety and avoidance of socializing situations

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Repeatedly assuming in sessions that others will see her as 'strange' and unwilling to befriend, attributing the inner fear of being rejected to peers' future reactions

positive_force: Good high school grades, possessing academic ability and adaptation resources
Close relationships with family, a potential support network exists
Willing to seek counseling and try evidence questioning and thought restructuring
negative_force: Highly sensitive to others' evaluations, tending toward mind reading and predicting a negative future
Avoiding social situations, leading to limited adaptation
Negating existing positive evidence, reinforcing worry and lonely anticipation

antecedent: Thinking about making new friends in college
Social cues as the start of college approaches
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being judged and rejected over small differences like disliking spaghetti, producing catastrophizing and negative predictions, trying to lower the risk of being rejected and anxiety through avoidance
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential negative evaluation and discomfort, temporarily relieving anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced socializing participation, affecting college adjustment and relationship building

target_behavior.behavior: Sleep difficulties (difficulty falling asleep, recurring worries)
antecedent: Thinking of college social life and others' evaluations before sleep
Time pressure as the school term approaches
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of being rejected and loneliness activated, negative automatic thoughts maintaining high vigilance and anxiety
target_behavior.function: Maintaining vigilance to (subjectively) prevent the imagined risk of being rejected, avoiding facing anxious feelings
target_behavior.consequence: Declining sleep quality, daytime functioning affected, anxiety further worsened
